value:
Confirm gate vs key spelling — #234, merged 2026-11-25 (272d70c). A key maps to its filename, so WHICH SPELLINGS REACH AN ENTRY IS THE FILESYSTEM'S RULE, NOT OURS: case on default macOS/Windows; APFS also folds Unicode (U+017F long s for s, the fi ligature, sharp s for ss, NFD for NFC); HFS+, exFAT and FAT fold case and normalization only. A flag matched by exact spelling let the flagged command run unasked under any other spelling that opens its file. THREE APPROACHES, TWO DROPPED after an independent review each — both had passed ~1,950 tests and a mutation check first. (1) Compare flag names with toLowerCase: misses the Unicode folds, and making list MUTATIONS case-insensitive stripped flags from entries that never moved (ops.* vs OPS.* are two namespaces; the same key in the other store). (2) Exact reads — getOne asking realpath, then readdir, what the opened file is called: realpath returns the name it was last GIVEN after a rename onto another spelling (APFS), listings return NFD on HFS+ and exFAT, and exact pre-reads removed the accidental 'already exists' refusal for a write to a fold spelling. Reverted; reads are main's. (3) SHIPPED: compare FILES, not names — fs.statSync with bigint, dev:ino of the key's entry path against each flagged key's path, per store dir (src/utils/entryIdentity.ts; one pass for many keys in entriesOpenedBy). Probed on APFS case-insensitive and case-sensitive, HFS+, exFAT, FAT32: 'same file' is true exactly when the spelling opens the stored file, also after a rewrite through the other spelling. RULES (owner decisions 2026-11-25): asking whether a key is gated is generous (name case aside, or same file). Changing the list is exact — a flag goes only under the name it is listed as, by `confirm remove` / --no-confirm or with the removal of that entry. A RENAME NEVER REMOVES A FLAG, it only adds the new key's: a flag gates by name and the global list is read in every project, so the old name's flag may be what gates another project's entry, which the rename cannot see (review found `rename -G <namespace>` ungating another project). `confirm set` refuses only a key that names no entry in either store, and a namespace; another spelling of an entry and an unreadable entry are accepted. THE TEST FOR ANY GATE CHANGE: every entry the old build gates is still gated on the new one after any command. Run it as a differential — the same random sequence of set / confirm set / confirm remove / rename / remove / copy / alias commands on both builds, over two projects, a directory outside any project and one shared global store, with keys that differ by case and by Unicode form; then for every key, from each directory, in default and global scope, evaluate the run gate with each build's own modules; a hit is old=GATED, new=not. That harness found what unit tests and 42 caught mutations did not. It is kept in scripts/gate-differential/ (README there; four command mixes, a replay for refused `confirm set`, and the filesystem probe behind the same-file comparison); it is not in `bun run test` and needs two builds. Self-review did not catch any of the three rounds of regressions; a reviewer in its own worktree, told to break it, did each time. The last commits (the owner's decisions) merged without such a review.

SINCE #234 (merged 2026-11-25/26, #264 #265 #269 #276; read before changing any of it):
- EITHER LIST GATES: only `true` is taken from each store's list; a project list cannot turn a global flag off (#241).
- A REMOVAL NEVER REMOVES A FLAG (#244): rm warns and names what stays; only `confirm remove` clears one, exactly.
- RENAME is one update() under both store locks, project first (#259). It refuses: an unreadable list in either store (#245); a source spelled other than its stored key, as the filesystem decides (#247); a leaf+namespace pair among the moved keys.
- WHERE `confirm set` LISTS (#255/#256): under the entry's STORED spelling, and under every spelling when project and global spell it differently. A global-only entry's flag goes in the GLOBAL list, which every rename sees. If the global list is unusable (unwritable, unreadable, a write error) it falls back to the project list with a warning; only -G refuses (owner decision).
- ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCES (owner): an explicit removal fully ungates where 1.3.0 kept a duplicate spelling; `confirm remove -G` clears a flag #256 put in the global list. Differential trials that show them: all-commands seed 202 #79/#107, seed 97 #126.
- MCP confirm_token is bound to a fingerprint of the previewed command plus every key it reaches (#243). Exec output is never re-scanned; output with shell syntax refuses the run (#242).
- Process that converged: one independent review plus one confirmation pass per PR (owner rule for 1.4.0); the reviewer must run its own differential seed and a case-sensitive disk image (hdiutil) for spelling changes — the stock harness never makes a store unwritable or uses mixed volumes.
- SINCE #292: the run gate checks every name a run looks up (#279), a --chain entry itself is gated, refs resolve in their entry's store (#280), and a stopped reference walk gates (#289) — see [[arch.interpolation]]. Since #288 an irregular _confirm.json (dir, symlink, mode 000) gates every run.
- HARNESS BLIND SPOT (#290): scripts/gate-differential/probe.mjs re-implements the gate and never runs runKeys/runGated, chains or MCP. The reviewers' end-to-end fuzzer (CLI and MCP, every command appends a marker, scored on what executed) is what found #289; plan step 1 brings it into the repo.
